question.text: A particle starts from origin at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> with a velocity <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> and moves in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi><mo>-</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">y</mi></math> plane under action of a force which produces a constant acceleration of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>(</mo><mn>3</mn><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">j</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>)</mo><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>. If the <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math>-coordinate of the particle at that instant is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>84</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>, then the speed of the particle at this time is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msqrt><mi>α</mi></msqrt><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>α</mi></math> is _______.

solution.text:
Given, ux=5 m s-1, ax=3 m s-2, x=84 m

The formula to calculate the velocity of the particle along x-axis is given by

vx2=ux2+2ax   ...1

From equation (1), it follows that

vx2=25+2(3)(84)⇒vx=23 m s-1

Also, the velocity of the particle along x-axis can be written as

vx=ux+axt   ...2

From equation (2), it follows that

t=23-53=6 s

Similarly, for the y- component of the velocity, it follows that

vy=0+ayt=0+2×(6)=12 m s-1

Hence, the magnitude of the velocity is given by

v2=vx2+vy2=232+122=673v=673 m s-1

Therefore, α=673.
